title: XRP Analyst Maps 61-Day Window for Next Macro Bottom as Cycle Gaps Halve
text:
XRP Analyst Maps 61-Day Window for Next Macro Bottom as Cycle Gaps Halve — BigGo Finance Ask AI Real-time News Market Earnings Call Event Calendar Watchlist Podcast Earnings Call Event Calendar Watchlist Podcast More Ask AI Real-time News Watchlist Holdings Market Earnings Call Event Calendar Podcast XRP Analyst Maps 61-Day Window for Next Macro Bottom as Cycle Gaps Halve
 Add preferred source An independent analyst publishing as Egrag Crypto has released a monthly-chart study of XRP examining how macro bottoms aligned with a bearish crossover of the 21-month EMA and 33-period MA. In the first cycle the bottom came 244 days after the crossover; in the second it came 122 days before, halving the gap and reversing its direction. Applying the same 50% compression yields a 61-day window for the third cycle, with candidate dates running from August 2026 to June 2027 if the crossover occurs in October 2026. XRP has already dropped about 61% to $1.28. The analyst outlines a bullish case with $1.25 as the floor, an intermediate case sweeping $1.20, $1.13 and $1.07, and a bearish case exposing $0.80 below $1.07, while cautioning that only two cycles exist and price action must confirm. Key Elements 
 XRP Egrag Crypto 21-month EMA 33-period MA Expanded Flat pattern An independent chart analyst who goes by Egrag Crypto has published a monthly-timeframe study of XRP that tracks how the token's macro bottoms lined up against a bearish crossover of the 21-month exponential moving average and the 33-period moving average, and uses the pattern to sketch a timing window for the next cycle.
 The core of the work is a comparison of two completed cycles. In the first, XRP's macro bottom arrived 244 days after the two averages crossed. In the second, the bottom came 122 days before the crossover, halving the gap and flipping its direction, so that the crossover confirmed a low already in place rather than preceding it.
 Carrying the halving one step further produces a 61-day window for the third cycle, with the bottom potentially forming either before or after the crossover. The analyst flagged the reversal between the first two cycles as a reason to treat the projection cautiously.
 Assuming the crossover lands in October 2026, the study lists five approximate dates for a macro bottom:
 Window Timing relative to crossover 
 August 2026 61 days before 
 December 2026 61 days after 
 February 2027 122 days, repeating the Cycle 2 gap 
 April 2027 Midpoint between 122 and 244 days 
 June 2027 244 days, repeating the Cycle 1 gap 
 Note: Windows are derived from the analyst's 50% compression method applied to two prior cycles.
 XRP has already fallen roughly 61%, from $3.30 to $1.28, which raises the question of whether the bearish crossover is simply ratifying a correction that has already played out. Moving averages are lagging indicators, and the study treats that lag as central to reading the current setup.
 The analyst lays out three paths from here. In the bullish case, $1.25 holds as the cycle low, higher lows take shape and XRP recovers its monthly moving averages. An intermediate scenario envisions a liquidity sweep below $1.25 that would open up $1.20, $1.13 and $1.07, levels tied to an Expanded Flat projection. Under the bearish case, a sustained close beneath $1.07 would leave the $0.80 area exposed to further losses.
 The study closes on a note of restraint. Only two historical cycles are available to work with, and the 50% compression and 61-day projection are described as mathematical observations rather than an established rule of timing. "Price action must confirm," the analyst wrote.
 For traders watching XRP's long-term structure, the takeaway is less a date certain than a set of boundaries: the halving pattern suggests the next bottom could cluster far more tightly around the crossover than in prior cycles, but the direction of that relationship has already flipped once, and the levels at $1.25 and $1.07 serve as the dividing lines between the three scenarios.
